ideas.title: Phantom Coast
ideas.status: exploratory hunch; not a registered hypothesis
ideas.question: Can a few false local reports create a persistent false coastline in a communicating Jev swarm?
ideas.comparison: Cross localized false reports versus equally sized random errors with independent decisions, neighbor exchange and source-aware exchange; hold distinct evidence and total calls fixed.
ideas.prediction: Local communication may amplify a spatially concentrated error; source-aware exchange may contain it.
ideas.falsifier: Reject the collective-amplification claim if errors do not spread beyond directly exposed cells or are fully predicted by the single-agent dose response.
ideas.confounds: Memorized geography, spatial autocorrelation, unequal evidence, and an incorrect map definition. A coordinate grid is not an image.
ideas.decision_value: Tests whether a distributed evidence map needs provenance-aware communication, independent of whether Jev can already recall Earth.
ideas.feasibility: Design sketch only; qualify a pinned model and publish a registered plan before any calls. No experiment implemented or run.

ideas.title: Quorum of Mirrors
ideas.status: exploratory hunch; not a registered hypothesis
ideas.question: How much independent information does a swarm of identical decision models actually contribute?
ideas.comparison: Compare repeated identical Jev calls, meaning-preserving prompt variants and disjoint evidence packets at equal calls; include a single solver with the union of evidence and dependency-aware aggregation.
metrics: Residual error correlation within difficulty strata
ideas.prediction: Evidence diversity may help more than cosmetic prompt diversity, but pooling can erase that advantage.
ideas.falsifier: Do not claim useful diversity if gains vanish against a single solver with matched evidence or only arise from more tokens.
ideas.confounds: Task difficulty creates apparent correlation; repeated calls share weights and data; majority agreement is not correctness.
ideas.decision_value: Decides whether to pay for more copies, more evidence, or an independent measurement.

ideas.title: The Right Dissenter (Stop-Signal Swarm)
ideas.status: exploratory hunch; not a registered hypothesis
ideas.question: Can a minority earn a bounded independent check that repairs wrong consensus without causing harmful reversals or repeated interruption?
ideas.comparison: Compare evidence-gated checks with majority, unconditional veto, always-check, quota-matched random checking, pooled evidence and an exact synthetic reference across provenance, applicability and temporal-change scenarios.
ideas.prediction: Targeted inhibition may contain bad cascades, but excessive inhibition may suppress valid new information.
ideas.falsifier: Drop the biological-mechanism claim if random throttling or simple rate limits achieve the same tradeoff.
ideas.confounds: A guaranteed-correct dissenter, oracle verification, unequal new evidence, stale-record persistence, uncounted deferrals and selection of only wrong-majority episodes can all manufacture improvement.
ideas.decision_value: Determines whether to implement a distinct evidence-backed stop channel rather than merely slowing communication.
ideas.feasibility: RD-1 plan and offline implementation under dissent/. Native execution remains gated; no measured Jev result.
ideas.delta: Honeybee cross-inhibition is direct biological prior. The Jev test concerns model-generated contradiction judgments with non-oracle evidence, beyond generic dissent.
ideas.source_note: RD-1 at researchers/vishesh/notes/dissent/PLAN.md. Earlier score is historical and becomes stale after this content revision.

assessment.rationale: Honeybee cross-inhibition is direct biological prior. The Jev test concerns model-generated contradiction judgments with non-oracle evidence, beyond generic dissent.

ideas.title: Panic Queue
ideas.status: exploratory hunch; not a registered hypothesis
ideas.question: Can uncertainty spread through a decision swarm and exhaust its ability to review legitimate work?
ideas.comparison: Replay paired clean and bounded-corruption decision streams through a finite reviewer queue; compare fixed confidence thresholds, queue-aware admission and reserved review capacity at equal service capacity.
metrics: Correct on-time completions over all arrivals
ideas.prediction: A small amount of ambiguous content may increase escalation enough to reduce total useful work even when accepted-answer accuracy looks safe.
ideas.falsifier: Drop the collective contribution if a standard queue fed the measured single-item escalation rates explains the entire effect and no communication-dependent residual remains.
ideas.confounds: Arrival rate and reviewer speed can manufacture overload. Include matched load without semantic corruption and score rejected tasks.
ideas.decision_value: Sets review-capacity and admission policies for fast decision services; distinguishes safer predictions from a functioning system.
ideas.feasibility: Design sketch only; qualify a pinned model and publish a registered plan before any calls. No experiment implemented or run.

ideas.title: Menu Parasites
ideas.status: exploratory hunch; not a registered hypothesis
ideas.question: Can harmless-looking changes to a choice menu redirect a collective even when underlying actions and evidence are unchanged?
ideas.comparison: Hold latent actions fixed while varying aliases, redundant options and order. Compare raw Choice, deduplicated canonical IDs and separate binary judgments with an explicit none/abstain option.
ideas.prediction: Equivalent option expansions may alter probabilities or downstream allocation; canonicalization may restore invariance.
ideas.falsifier: If all change is predicted by probability normalization or disappears after aggregating aliases, report a harness arithmetic effect rather than semantic manipulation.
ideas.confounds: Equivalent alternatives may legitimately split probability. Choice confidence depends on menu size; use a fixed-action null model.
ideas.decision_value: Tests whether tool registries and shared action catalogs require canonicalization before decision-model calls.
